title: Quasi-coherent sheaves on prestacks
summary: The functor-of-points theory of quasi-coherent sheaves: QCoh(X) as the limit of module infinity-categories over the affine points of a prestack, for classical, animated and connective E-infinity test rings over Z, with the coherent module functor and module theory of connective algebras, flat hyperdescent without finiteness hypotheses, invariance under fpqc sheafification, affine pushforward with base change, the comparison with quasi-coherent derived sheaves of every Mathlib scheme, the t-structure and perfect and almost perfect objects, quotients by group prestacks and discrete groups, classical quotient stacks, and compact generation and perfect stacks.

targets.name: Prestack.TestRings
targets.statement: The three infinity-categories of test rings CRing (nerve of CommRingCat), AnRing (AnimAlg_Z) and CAlg^cn = CAlg(D(Z)_{>=0}), linked by iota : CRing -> AnRing (discrete animated rings) and theta : AnRing -> CAlg^cn; homotopy groups pi_n A of a test ring, pi_0 A an ordinary commutative ring.
hypotheses: u is a fixed universe and test rings are u-small

locator.where: Definition 6.2.2.1 and Remark 6.2.2.2, pp. 490-491; HA Proposition 7.1.3.18, p. 1219

api.name: pi_theta
api.statement: pi_*(theta B) = pi_*(B), and theta(iota R) is discrete with pi_0 = R.

api.name: theta_preservesColimits
api.statement: theta preserves small colimits, in particular pushouts and finite products.

api.name: iota_fullyFaithful
api.statement: iota is fully faithful with left adjoint pi_0, so it preserves limits.

api.name: pushout_tor
api.statement: For discrete A, B, C the derived pushout has pi_n = Tor_n^A(B, C); the CRing pushout is the ordinary tensor product.

api.name: initial_final
api.statement: The zero ring is final and Z is initial in each of the three categories.

tests.name: fp_tensor_fp
tests.statement: F_p (x)_Z F_p in AnRing has pi_0 = pi_1 = F_p and no other homotopy; theta preserves it; the CRing pushout is F_p, so iota does not preserve pushouts.

tests.name: zero_ring
tests.statement: The zero ring is final in all three, theta(iota 0) = 0 and pi_*(0) = 0.

tests.name: theta_not_equivalence
tests.statement: theta(Z[x]) is discrete, whereas the free object of CAlg^cn on Z[0] has the summand (Z (x)^L Z)_{h Sigma_2} with pi_1 = H_1(B Sigma_2; Z) = Z/2.

targets.name: Prestack.moduleFunctor
targets.statement: The functor Mod : CAlg^cn -> CAlg(PrL_st), A |-> Mod_A(D(Z)) with unit A and extension of scalars as transitions; its restrictions along theta and theta iota are animatedModules and R |-> D_infty(R).
hypotheses: D(Z) is presentably symmetric monoidal stable with tensor preserving colimits in each variable

locator.where: Theorem 4.5.3.1 and Remark 4.5.3.2, p. 601; Corollary 4.8.5.21, p. 754; Theorem 4.8.4.6, p. 737

api.name: restriction_adjoint
api.statement: For f : A -> B, f^* is symmetric monoidal and colimit-preserving with a conservative colimit-preserving right adjoint f_*; projection formula f_*(f^*M (x)_B N) = M (x)_A f_*N.

api.name: baseChange
api.statement: For a pushout square of CAlg^cn the square of extension functors is right adjointable, and Mod_{B'} = Mod_B (x)_{Mod_A} Mod_{A'}.

api.name: products
api.statement: Mod_{A x B} = Mod_A x Mod_B symmetric monoidally and Mod_0 = 0.

api.name: classicalValues
api.statement: Mod_{theta iota R} = D_infty(R) naturally in R, with transitions the derived base change.

tests.name: unit_zero
tests.statement: Mod_Z = D_infty(Z) with unit Z[0] and Mod_0 = 0.

tests.name: fp_baseChange
tests.statement: For the pushout of Z -> F_p with itself in CAlg^cn both sides of base change at N = F_p are F_p (x)^L_Z F_p with pi_1 = F_p; with the ordinary pushout F_p the square is not right adjointable.

tests.name: projectionFormula_shift
tests.statement: For R -> R[t], M = R[1], N = R[t] both sides are the R-module R[t][1].

tests.name: classical_transition
tests.statement: The transition along Z -> Z/p sends Z/p to Z/p (x)^L Z/p with pi_0 = pi_1 = Z/p, unlike the underived extension.

targets.name: Prestack.Mod.tStructure
targets.statement: For A in CAlg^cn, (Mod_A^cn, Mod_{A,<=0}) is an accessible t-structure on Mod_A, left and right complete, both halves closed under products and filtered colimits, heart = ModuleCat(pi_0 A), Mod_A^cn generated by A under colimits; for flat N, pi_n(M (x)_A N) = pi_n M (x)_{pi_0 A} pi_0 N; flat and faithfully flat maps as in HA 7.2.2.10.
hypotheses: A is a connective commutative algebra of D(Z)

locator.where: Proposition 7.1.1.13, p. 1202; Definition 7.2.2.10, Proposition 7.2.2.13 and Theorem 7.2.2.15, pp. 1240-1241

api.name: rightTExact
api.statement: Extension of scalars is right t-exact and restriction of scalars is t-exact.

api.name: flat_tExact
api.statement: Extension along a flat map is t-exact; along a faithfully flat map it is moreover conservative.

api.name: flat_stable
api.statement: Flat and faithfully flat maps are stable under composition and base change; iota and theta preserve and reflect them.

api.name: lazard
api.statement: A connective module is flat iff it is a filtered colimit of finite free modules.

api.name: flat_classical
api.statement: For discrete A and M flatness is Mathlib's Module.Flat.

tests.name: heart_derived_intersection
tests.statement: The heart of Mod_{F_p (x)^L F_p} is ModuleCat F_p although its unit has pi_1 = F_p.

tests.name: fracture_ff
tests.statement: Z -> Z[1/p] x Z_p is faithfully flat.

tests.name: Q_not_ff
tests.statement: Z -> Q is flat and not faithfully flat: Q (x)^L Z/p = 0.

tests.name: nonflat_not_texact
tests.statement: Extension along Z -> F_p sends the discrete F_p to F_p (x)^L F_p, not discrete.

targets.name: Prestack.Mod.Perf
targets.statement: Perfect modules (thick subcategory generated by A), almost perfect modules (bounded below and almost compact), locally free modules of finite rank (summands of A^n) over A in CAlg^cn; perfect = compact = dualizable; stability under base change; comparison with DerivedModuleAlgebra predicates for discrete A.
hypotheses: A is a connective commutative algebra of D(Z)

api.name: perf_compact_dualizable
api.statement: Mod_A is compactly generated by A and perfect = compact = dualizable.

api.name: aperf_closure
api.statement: Almost perfect modules form a stable retract-closed subcategory containing the perfect ones; connective ones are realizations of degreewise finite free simplicial modules; coherent criterion of HA 7.2.4.17.

api.name: locallyFree_dualizable
api.statement: A connective module is dualizable in Mod_A^cn iff it is locally free of finite rank (SAG Proposition 2.9.1.5).

api.name: baseChange_stable
api.statement: Connectivity, flatness, perfectness, almost perfectness and local freeness are stable under base change (SAG Proposition 6.2.5.2).

api.name: discrete_comparison
api.statement: For discrete A these are DerivedDeRham.IsPerfect, IsPseudoCoherent and HasTorAmplitude.

tests.name: Z_plus_Z3
tests.statement: Z (+) Z[3] is perfect with dual Z (+) Z[-3]; Q and (+)_N Z are not perfect.

tests.name: dual_numbers
tests.statement: k over k[e]/(e^2) is almost perfect but not perfect: Tor_i(k, k) = k for all i.

tests.name: infinite_poly
tests.statement: k = k[x_1, x_2, ...]/(x_i) is not almost perfect: the maximal ideal is not finitely generated.

tests.name: Zp_not_locally_free
tests.statement: Z/p over Z is connective and perfect but not locally free: its dual Z/p[-1] is not connective.

tests.name: truncation_unstable
tests.statement: F_p over Z is 0-truncated but its base change to F_p has pi_1 != 0.

targets.name: Prestack.limit_adjointable
targets.statement: (a) A natural transformation of diagrams K -> Cat_infty-hat with componentwise right adjoints and right adjointable naturality squares has a componentwise right adjoint on limits, and the projection squares are right adjointable. (b) Dualizable (invertible) objects of a limit of symmetric monoidal infinity-categories are those with dualizable (invertible) images. (c) Descent criterion: an augmented cosimplicial infinity-category satisfying Beck-Chevalley is a limit diagram iff C^{-1} -> C^0 is comonadic.
hypotheses: K is an infinity-category
for (c), each coface square is right adjointable

locator.where: Corollary 4.7.4.18, p. 699; Proposition 4.6.1.11, p. 620; Theorem 4.7.5.2 and Corollary 4.7.5.3, pp. 704-705; Proposition 5.2.2.36, p. 835

api.name: adjointable_limit
api.statement: Right adjoint of the limit computed componentwise, projection squares right adjointable.

api.name: dualizable_limit
api.statement: Dualizable and invertible objects of a limit are detected componentwise.

api.name: descent_criterion
api.statement: Beck-Chevalley plus comonadicity of C^{-1} -> C^0 gives C^{-1} = lim C^.

tests.name: empty_diagram
tests.statement: The empty limit is the zero category; its object is dualizable and invertible.

tests.name: product_dualizable
tests.statement: (Z, Q) in D(Z) x D(Z) is not dualizable; (Z, Z[1]) is invertible.

tests.name: non_adjointable
tests.statement: The ordinary pushout square of Z -> F_p with itself is not right adjointable; the limit right adjoint then is not componentwise.

tests.name: compact_not_componentwise
tests.statement: On B(Z/p) x Spec F_p the unit is componentwise compact but not compact (8.5).

targets.name: Prestack.Pts
targets.statement: PreStk_T = Fun(T, S-hat), Spec : T^op -> PreStk_T the Yoneda embedding, and the infinity-category of points Pts(X), the left fibration over T classified by X.
hypotheses: T is one of CRing, AnRing, CAlg^cn

locator.where: Notation 6.2.2.3 and Remark 6.2.2.7, pp. 491-492

api.name: yoneda
api.statement: Spec is fully faithful and Map(Spec A, X) = X(A).

api.name: pointwise_limits
api.statement: Limits and colimits of prestacks are pointwise; the empty prestack is initial and Spec Z is final.

api.name: coYoneda
api.statement: Every prestack is the colimit of Spec A over Pts(X)^op.

api.name: affine_fibreProduct
api.statement: Spec B x_{Spec A} Spec C = Spec(B (x)_A C) with the pushout of T.

tests.name: pts_initial
tests.statement: Pts(Spec A) has the initial object (A, id); for the constant prestack B Gamma the points retain pi_1 = Gamma.

tests.name: spec_zero
tests.statement: Spec 0 is not the empty prestack but becomes equivalent to it after fpqc sheafification.

tests.name: fibre_product_context
tests.statement: In CRing Spec F_p x_{Spec Z} Spec F_p = Spec F_p; in AnRing it is Spec(F_p (x)^L F_p).

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh
targets.statement: QCoh : PreStk_T^op -> CAlg(Cat_infty-hat), the right Kan extension of Spec A |-> Mod_A along Spec, QCoh(X) = lim over Pts(X) of Mod_A; evaluation eta^*, pullback f^*, structure sheaf O_X.
hypotheses: T is one of the three contexts

locator.where: Definition 6.2.2.1, pp. 490-491; Remarks 6.2.2.5 and 6.2.2.7, pp. 491-492; Section 6.2.6 and Notation 6.2.6.1, pp. 496-497; GR-I Chapter I.3, Section 1.1, p. 143

api.name: affineValue
api.statement: QCoh(Spec A) = Mod_A symmetric monoidally and naturally in A.

api.name: pullback_functorial
api.statement: (fg)^* = g^* f^* and id^* = id coherently; eta^* is pullback along eta.

api.name: objects
api.statement: Objects are modules F(eta) with coherent equivalences B (x)_A F(eta) = F(phi eta); eta^* O_X = A.

api.name: mappingSpaces
api.statement: Map(F, G) = lim Map_{Mod_A}(F(eta), G(eta)).

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: QCoh(empty) is the zero category; a colimit formula would give the empty infinity-category.

tests.name: specZ
tests.statement: QCoh(Spec Z) = D_infty(Z) in each context.

tests.name: disjoint_union
tests.statement: QCoh(Spec A u Spec B) = Mod_A x Mod_B = Mod_{A x B}.

tests.name: BZ2_class
tests.statement: On B(Z/2) x Spec F_2, pi_0 Map(O, O[1]) = H^1(Z/2; F_2) = F_2 while its pullback to the atlas point is 0.

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.formal
targets.statement: QCoh carries small colimits of prestacks to limits; QCoh(X) is stable with small colimits computed pointwise; f^* preserves small colimits and is symmetric monoidal; tensor is pointwise and preserves colimits in each variable; equivalences and zero objects are detected pointwise; QCoh(X) is presentable for X a u-small colimit of affines; in CRing the homotopy category of QCoh(Spec R) is DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R) with shift and triangles.
hypotheses: X is a prestack on one of the three contexts
for presentability, X is a u-small colimit of affines

api.name: colimits_to_limits
api.statement: QCoh(colim X_i) = lim QCoh(X_i).

api.name: stable_colimits
api.statement: QCoh(X) is stable with pointwise small colimits; f^* is colimit-preserving and symmetric monoidal.

api.name: pointwise_tensor
api.statement: (F (x) G)(eta) = F(eta) (x)_A G(eta).

api.name: conservative
api.statement: A map is an equivalence iff all evaluations are.

api.name: homotopyCategory
api.statement: ho QCoh(Spec R) = DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R) with shift and triangles.

tests.name: Zp_tensor
tests.statement: On Spec Z, Z/p (x) Z/p has pi_0 = pi_1 = Z/p.

tests.name: one_point_insufficient
tests.statement: On B(Z/2) x Spec F_2 the nonzero O -> O[1] vanishes at the atlas point.

tests.name: presentable_BGamma
tests.statement: QCoh(B Gamma x Spec k) = Fun(B Gamma, Mod_k) is presentable.

tests.name: ext1_Z
tests.statement: Hom(Z/p, Z/p[1]) = Ext^1(Z/p, Z/p) = Z/p in ho QCoh(Spec Z).

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.leftKanInvariance
targets.statement: For u in {iota, theta, theta iota}, u_! the left Kan extension of prestacks, QCoh(u_! X) = QCoh(X) symmetric monoidally and naturally in X, compatibly with pullback and evaluation; u_! Spec A = Spec u(A).
hypotheses: the module functor of the source is that of the target restricted along u

locator.where: Remark 6.2.2.2, p. 491; GR-I Chapter I.3, Section 1.2, pp. 145-146

api.name: adjunction
api.statement: u_! is left adjoint to restriction u^*.

api.name: representables
api.statement: u_! Spec A = Spec u(A) and u_! preserves colimits.

api.name: not_fibreProducts
api.statement: u_! does not preserve fibre products: iota_! of the classical Spec F_p x_{Spec Z} Spec F_p is Spec F_p, not Spec(F_p (x)^L F_p).

tests.name: yoneda_case
tests.statement: u_! Spec R = Spec u(R) and u_!(empty) = empty.

tests.name: restriction_fails
tests.statement: For Y = Spec(F_p (x)^L F_p), iota^* Y = Spec F_p with QCoh = D(F_p), whereas the unit of QCoh(Y) has pi_1 = F_p.

tests.name: constant_prestack
tests.statement: iota_! of the classical B Gamma x Spec F_2 is the animated one, both with QCoh = Fun(B Gamma, D(F_2)).

targets.name: Prestack.ofScheme
targets.statement: The classical prestack h_X of a Mathlib scheme X, R |-> Hom(Spec R, X), and the classical prestack X^natural of a SchemeAndStackFoundations stack in groupoids, by straightening the nerve of its Grothendieck construction over affines; h is fully faithful; compatibility with 2-fibre products and with stackification versus sheafification.
hypotheses: X a Mathlib scheme, or a StackInGroupoids of SchemeAndStackFoundations section 1.18

locator.where: Proposition 2.1.1.3 (PDF p. 75) and Proposition 1.2.5.1 (PDF p. 53)

api.name: h_fullyFaithful
api.statement: h is fully faithful and h_{Spec R} = Spec R.

api.name: value_nerve
api.statement: X^natural(R) is the nerve of the groupoid X(Spec R), a Kan complex.

api.name: fibreProducts
api.statement: (-)^natural carries 2-fibre products to fibre products of prestacks.

api.name: stackification
api.statement: (-)^natural carries fppf stackification to fppf sheafification of 1-truncated prestacks.

tests.name: spec_case
tests.statement: h_{Spec R} = Spec R; restriction to fields is not faithful on Spec k[e].

tests.name: BZ2_real
tests.statement: For G = Z/2, (BG)^natural(R-real) has two components and pi_1 = Z/2 at the trivial torsor; over R x R it has pi_1 = (Z/2)^2.

tests.name: pi0_loses
tests.statement: Replacing groupoids by isomorphism classes gives a point on strictly henselian local rings and loses pi_1 = G(R).

targets.name: Prestack.fpqcTopology
targets.statement: The fpqc topology on T^op by finite families with faithfully flat product, flat hypercovers (latching maps faithfully flat), fpqc sheaves and hypercomplete sheaves, and the (hyper)sheafification L, with its universal property for limit-preserving functors.
hypotheses: T is one of the three contexts

locator.where: Remark D.6.1.1 and Definition D.6.1.4, pp. 2173-2174; Proposition 1.3.1.7, p. 117

api.name: stability
api.statement: Covers and flat hypercovers are stable under base change and composition; iota and theta preserve covers and Cech nerves.

api.name: mathlib_comparison
api.statement: In CRing a family is a cover iff the Spec family is an fpqcPrecoverage covering.

api.name: sheafification
api.statement: L is left exact and preserves colimits.

api.name: universal_property
api.statement: A limit-preserving functor on PreStk^op inverts L-equivalences iff its restriction to T^op is a (hypercomplete) sheaf.

tests.name: empty_cover
tests.statement: The empty family covers exactly the zero ring.

tests.name: zariski_fracture
tests.statement: {Z -> Z[1/2], Z -> Z[1/3]} and Z -> Z[1/p] x Z_p are covers; R -> C is a finite etale cover.

tests.name: non_covers
tests.statement: Z -> F_p (not flat) and Z -> Q (not faithfully flat) are not covers.

targets.name: Prestack.Mod.flatHyperdescent
targets.statement: For A in CAlg^cn and every flat hypercover A -> A_., Mod_A^cn -> lim Mod^cn_{A_.} and Mod_A -> lim_{Delta_s} Mod_{A_.} are equivalences, the second symmetric monoidal; Mod is a hypercomplete fpqc sheaf; M = lim M (x)_A A_n; the same for AnRing and CRing; no finiteness, countability or descendability hypothesis.
hypotheses: A is connective
A -> A_. is a flat hypercover

locator.where: Theorem D.6.3.1 and Corollaries D.6.3.3-D.6.3.4, pp. 2177-2178; Propositions D.6.1.3 and D.6.2.3, pp. 2174-2177; GR-I Chapter I.3, Theorem 1.3.4 and Corollary 1.3.5, pp. 146-147

api.name: descendable_agreement
api.statement: For descendable faithfully flat maps the equivalence agrees with moduleDescent.

api.name: hearts
api.statement: On hearts Cech descent is ordinary module descent, the affine case of qcoh_fpqc_descent.

api.name: sheaf
api.statement: Mod is a hypercomplete CAlg(Cat_infty-hat)-valued fpqc sheaf on T^op in each context.

tests.name: identity
tests.statement: For A -> A the Cech nerve is constant and the totalization is Mod_A.

tests.name: zariski
tests.statement: For (f, g) = A, Mod_A = Mod_{A_f} x_{Mod_{A_fg}} Mod_{A_g}; two-term complexes glue with their differential.

tests.name: fracture
tests.statement: Z -> Z[1/p] x Z_p recovers D(Z) and Z = Z[1/p] x_{Q_p} Z_p.

tests.name: Fp_not_cover
tests.statement: Z -> F_p kills Q, so descent fails.

tests.name: dual_numbers
tests.statement: F_p -> F_p[e]/(e^2) is faithfully flat and descent recovers Mod_{F_p}; the reduction map is not a cover.

tests.name: zariski_descendable
tests.statement: A finite Zariski cover is descendable and the two descent equivalences coincide.

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.sheafificationEquiv
targets.statement: (a) f^* is an equivalence for every map that becomes an equivalence after fpqc hypersheafification; (b) QCoh on hypercomplete fpqc sheaves carries small colimits to limits; (c) Cech descent along fpqc surjections; (d) fppf, etale and Zariski descent.
hypotheses: T is one of the three contexts

locator.where: Proposition 6.2.3.1 and Remarks 6.2.3.2-6.2.3.3, p. 492; GR-I Chapter I.3, Corollaries 1.3.7, 1.3.8 and 1.3.11, p. 147

api.name: sheafification_invariance
api.statement: QCoh(LX) = QCoh(X) for sheafification and hypersheafification.

api.name: cech
api.statement: QCoh(X) = lim QCoh(U_n) for the Cech nerve of an fpqc surjection U -> X.

tests.name: local_equivalences
tests.statement: QCoh(Spec 0) = 0 = QCoh(empty) and Mod_{A x B} = Mod_A x Mod_B.

tests.name: Fp_not_surjection
tests.statement: Spec F_p -> Spec Z is not an fpqc surjection and its Cech totalization kills Q.

tests.name: BGamma_torsors
tests.statement: For finite Gamma the constant prestack B Gamma x Spec k and the stack of Gamma-torsors have QCoh = Fun(B Gamma, Mod_k).

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.zariskiGluing
targets.statement: (a) For a Mathlib scheme X, QCoh(h_X) = lim over affine opens of QCoh(Spec O(U)), and = lim over a Zariski hypercover by disjoint unions of affine opens; (b) QCoh(X) is presentable when LX lies in the colimit closure of representables in hypercomplete fpqc sheaves.
hypotheses: X a Mathlib scheme for (a)
LX in the u-small colimit closure of representables for (b)

locator.where: Chapter I.3, Proposition 1.4.4, p. 149; SAG Proposition 6.2.3.4(3), p. 493

api.name: affine_open_limit
api.statement: QCoh(h_X) = lim over affine opens.

api.name: presentable
api.statement: QCoh(X) presentable for X in the colimit closure of representables.

tests.name: P1
tests.statement: QCoh(h_{P^1}) = D(k[t]) x_{D(k[t,t^-1])} D(k[t^-1]); pi_0 Map(O, O(-2)[1]) = k spanned by t^-1.

tests.name: infinite_disjoint_union
tests.statement: QCoh of the coproduct of countably many Spec Z is the product of D(Z), presentable.

tests.name: empty_scheme
tests.statement: For the empty scheme QCoh = 0.

targets.name: Prestack.IsAffineMorphism
targets.statement: A map f : Y -> X of prestacks is affine if every base change to an affine point is affine, Spec f_eta; flat affine if each A -> f_eta is flat.
hypotheses: fibre products in the given context (ordinary in CRing)

api.name: stability
api.statement: Affine morphisms are stable under composition and base change and contain maps between affines.

api.name: colimit_presentation
api.statement: For f affine, Y = colim Spec f_eta over Pts(X)^op.

tests.name: identity_affines
tests.statement: id_X and Spec B -> Spec A are affine.

tests.name: punctured_plane
tests.statement: h of A^2 minus 0 -> h of A^2 is not affine.

tests.name: BG
tests.statement: For a nontrivial affine group scheme G over k, Spec k -> BG is affine with fibre G, whereas BG -> Spec k is not: BG at the discrete test ring O(G) has pi_1 = G(O(G)), containing id != 1, while affines take discrete values on discrete test rings. For G = 1 both maps are the identity, which is affine.

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.affinePushforward
targets.statement: For f affine (flat affine in CRing), f^* has a pointwise right adjoint f_* (restriction of scalars at each point), f_* preserves small colimits, the projection formula holds, and the Beck-Chevalley map is an equivalence for every pullback square in the context.
hypotheses: f affine
in the classical context f flat affine

locator.where: Proposition 6.3.4.1 and Corollary 6.3.4.3, pp. 505-506; GR-I Chapter I.3, Proposition 2.2.2, p. 153

api.name: pointwise
api.statement: (f_* F)(eta) is the restriction of scalars of F(Y_eta).

api.name: baseChange
api.statement: g^* f_* -> f'_* g'^* is an equivalence for every pullback square in the context.

tests.name: identity
tests.statement: For f = id all statements are identities.

tests.name: affine_line
tests.statement: For Spec R[t] -> Spec R, f_* O = R[t] free of infinite rank; base change gives R'[t].

tests.name: classical_nonflat
tests.statement: For classical Spec F_p -> Spec Z with itself base change fails and the pointwise formula is wrong; in AnRing it holds.

tests.name: shifted_projection
tests.statement: With M = R[1], N = B both sides are B[1].

targets.name: Prestack.QCoh.specEquiv
targets.statement: For R in CRing, Phi_R : QCoh(Spec R) = Mod_{theta iota R} = D_infty(R) = Dqc(Spec R) is a symmetric monoidal equivalence natural in R for derived pullback; on homotopy categories it is DQCoh.affineEquiv and it carries tensor to derivedTensor.
hypotheses: R an ordinary commutative ring

locator.where: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.3.5, tag 06Z0; SAG Proposition 2.2.3.3, p. 202

api.name: naturality
api.statement: Phi_S o phi^* = L(Spec phi)^* o Phi_R coherently.

api.name: homotopyCategory
api.statement: On homotopy categories Phi_R is Coherent.DQCoh.affineEquiv.

api.name: tensor
api.statement: Phi_R carries the tensor product to derivedTensor.

tests.name: unit
tests.statement: O_{Spec R} goes to R[0]; (Z/2)[0] goes to (Z/2)~ supported at (2).

tests.name: derived_pullback
tests.statement: For Z -> F_p, Z/p goes to cohomology F_p in degrees 0 and -1; the underived pullback lacks degree -1.

tests.name: tensor_tor

targets.name: Prestack.IsPerfectStack.permanence
targets.statement: (a) Affine over perfect is perfect (classical: flat affine over perfect). (b) Classical: if f : Y -> X is flat and representable by qcqs schemes (5.4(b)), X is perfect, and a set {L_i} of invertible objects of QCoh(Y) restricts on every base change Y_eta to an ample family of invertible modules (Stacks tag 0FXR), then Y is perfect; one ample invertible object is the one-member case. (c) Animated, E-infinity: every morphism between perfect stacks has perfect base change along every point of the target; classical: every morphism representable by qcqs schemes with affine diagonal (every base change along a point a qcqs scheme with affine diagonal) has perfect base change along every point, with no flatness and no perfectness of source or target. (d) Animated, E-infinity: for perfect X_1, X_2 over Y with affine diagonal, X_1 x_Y X_2 is perfect (Y final: X_1 x X_2). Classical: if X_2 is perfect and X_1 -> Y is flat affine or of the kind in (b), then X_1 x_Y X_2 is perfect.
hypotheses: (a) f affine and X perfect; classical context: f flat affine
(b) classical context; f flat and representable by qcqs schemes; X perfect; {L_i} invertible objects of QCoh(Y) forming an ample family on every base change Y_eta along a point of X
(c) animated and E-infinity: source and target perfect; classical: the morphism representable by qcqs schemes with affine diagonal
(d) animated and E-infinity: X_1, X_2 perfect, Y with affine diagonal; classical: X_2 perfect, X_1 -> Y flat affine or of the kind in (b)

gaps.title: Chevalley's theorem: GL_n/H is quasi-projective
gaps.detail: For a field k, an affine group scheme H of finite type over k and a closed immersion H -> GL_n, the fppf quotient GL_n/H is represented by a quasi-projective k-scheme admitting a GL_n-equivariant immersion into the projectivization of a finite-dimensional representation, so that O(1) is a GL_n-linearized ample line bundle. Used in the proof of BZFN Corollary 3.22 (BZFN line 1205) to make BG perfect from BGL_n.
gaps.needs: A statement that the fppf quotient of GL_n by a closed subgroup scheme of finite type over a field is a quasi-projective scheme with a GL_n-equivariant immersion into the projectivization of a finite-dimensional representation.
